evidence: Product.create validates the id and initial stock and throws a domain ValidationError. This is a business invariant.
reserve/canReserve use the available stock to enforce the rule that stock cannot be over-reserved, throwing InsufficientStockError. This is domain logic.
dispatch/release change the stock state according to warehouse business rules.
restore/toSnapshot only map to and from a plain ProductSnapshot object. They contain no storage technology or I/O, so they are a domain memento, not persistence logic.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/domain/Product.ts is a pure domain entity. It holds stock state (onHand and reserved) and enforces business invariants: validation when the product is created, checking availability before a reservation, and the rules for release and dispatch. It raises domain errors. The ProductSnapshot type and the restore/toSnapshot methods are a plain-data memento. They use no persistence technology, ORM, SQL, serialization format or I/O, so the entity can be rebuilt without depending on infrastructure. Nothing in the file is transport, framework or application orchestration logic. Every responsibility fits the domain layer.
